title: Tecnimed S.r.l. v. Laboratoire Marque Verte S.A. (Cour d'appel de Paris)
parties: Tecnimed S.r.l. v. Laboratoire Marque Verte S.A.
abstract:
[Abstract prepared by Dott. Mira Ghazzoul, La Sapienza University of Rome]

An Italian manufacturer of medical devices entered a commercial relationship with a French company for the sale and distribution of some products, among which a thermometer called 'Visotemp'. In July 2015, the seller requested payment for a purchase order of thermometers allegedly received, but the buyer refused to confirm the order due to a bad sales forecast. In October 2016, the buyer informed the seller of its decision to suspend the distribution of the product. In October 2018, the seller sued the buyer, alleging that it was entitled to outstanding payments and damages resulting from the abrupt termination of the commercial relationship. The first instance tribunal found for the buyer. The seller appealed the decision.

After ascertaining that the Convention applied to the merits of the dispute under its Art. 1(1)(a), the Court found that, contrary to what contended by the seller, the communication by the buyer regarding 6,000 thermoters made at the beginning of April 2015 did not qualify as a purchase order, yet as a quote request, because indication of price was lacking. Consequently, it could not be treated as an offer within the meaning of Art. 14 CISG. Instead, the proforma invoice issued by the seller at the end of April 2015 in response to the request quote constituted a commercial offer. However, despite such an offer, no sales contract had been formed because the French party gave acceptance neither by an email communication nor effecting the requested down payment. Nor could it be possible – as contended by the seller – to treat silence by the buyer after three days had elapsed from the issuance of the proforma invoice as a manifestation of assent because, according to Art. 18 CISG, silence or inactivity does not in itself amount to acceptance.

In conclusion, the Appellate Court confirmed the first instance judgment and rejected the seller’s claim for damages.
keywords:
REQUIREMENTS FOR OFFER (ART. 14 CISG) - DETERMINATION OF PRICE

SILENCE OR INACTIVITY - DOES NOT AMOUNT TO ACCEPTANCE (ART. 18(1) CISG)
